title: R' Gurion

paragraphs: In Shabbat 33b: “R' Gurion — and some say Rav Yosef bar Shemayah — said: When there are righteous people in the generation, the righteous are seized for the generation.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5, folio 13b: R' Yonah went up to R' Guryan; he came out to him wearing a sandal (he was in mourning, and it was Shabbat). R' Yonah said to him: “What do you think — that we learn practice from you? We do not learn practice from a small person.” In Jerusalem Talmud Maaser Sheni 2:2 and Nazir, beginning of chapter 8: R' Guryan in the name of R' Yose bar Chanina. In Jerusalem Talmud Gittin, chapter 5 [halakhah supplied as ה״V], he spoke in the name of R-Sh-B-L; and in Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:1: “R' Gurion said: The Mundelai asked R-Sh-B-L.”

In Jerusalem Talmud Peah 3:9: R' Guryan’s sister wrote her property over to her brother; her elder brother went and appeased her — the case came before R' Imi. Hyman suggests that perhaps his brother is R' Menachem, who is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 9:8.

Hyman’s printed page (vol. I, p. 302) gives Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 5:5, where the supplied transcription has ה״V. In the Guggenheimer edition, the passage naming Rabbi Gurion in the name of Resh Lakish is at 5:6. In Megillah 3:1 that edition has the people of Magdala asking R’ Shimon ben Lakish where Hyman writes Mundelai. In Moed Katan 3:5 the consulted text reads Gurion and has sandals in the plural, with the episode marked 16a. The translation retains Hyman’s 13b locator and wording.

Hyman’s printed Peah locator is 3:9. The corresponding story appears at 3:7 in the Guggenheimer edition and at 3:7, folio 18b, in Machon Mamre. The story continues with a second conveyance and the ruling. The brother named Menachem in Bava Metzia 9:8 is explicit there. Linking him to this Peah episode remains Hyman’s suggestion.
